object_description: three building volumes of similar expression carrying an external triangular timber support structure
design_condition: the three volumes are united around a slightly raised schoolyard extending the existing square, so that the entrances are protected and detached from through traffic

positive: The composition gives the complex site environment a remarkable unity
Adequate relationships are created between public spaces, the residential quarters and the sports facilities in the park
The raised schoolyard protects the three entrances and detaches them from through traffic
The external triangular timber structure gives the public buildings an original identity for the whole district
The primary load-bearing structure can be read as a feature of the facade
Freedom from internal load-bearing elements gives unlimited flexibility
A school without corridors is created where every open space is habitable
The ratio of usable space to circulation area is optimal
The gymnasium benefits from views of the outside space on all four sides
Evening use casts light on the surrounding garden landscape and socialises the public space
The visible timber construction leads to a strong identity and maximises interior flexibility
Room layouts and divisions are simple and generally appropriate
All second-stage units of the basic level have direct access and clearly defined outdoor space
The location of the double gymnasium is ideal, with direct access for clubs
The sports room programme is complete and well organised
The facility is rated compact and good, including the space-saving floor plan layout
negative: The kindergarten rooms of the second construction phase have no direct connection to the outdoor spaces
The external timber load-bearing structure proves impossible in the long term as its exposed joints require extensive maintenance
The client cannot take the significant economic risk of this structural proposal
The schematic layouts produce tubular, insufficiently lit side rooms, particularly at base level
Acoustic closures hide the ceiling beams in wood, considerably reducing their pedagogical and acoustic value
Not all four first-stage units of the basic level have their own directly assigned outdoor space
The large static height of ribbed ceilings and beams results in a very large building volume
Countless timber connections in the facade and ceiling intersections lead to high construction costs
The load-bearing facade is exposed to snow and rain, and the low points of the V-supports collect water
The system requires complex penetrations of the main ceiling beams through the glass facade
Due to the large building volume the project is in the upper range of cost
